thread:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — a few enterprise customers asked for a "fan-out with conditional continue" primitive for tool calls. They want: fan out to several adapters, stop early if a validator approves, but also an aggregate mode. How do we shape the API + SLA? :thinking:

Ajay Patel: Can we get concrete customer flows? I heard two: 1) fraud validators in parallel -> first positive approves 2) enrichers called in parallel -> merge partial data and return best-effort.

Samir Gupta: Yup. Observed patterns:
- Approval (first-true shortcircuit)
- Merge (gather what's available within deadline)
- Quorum (need M of N successes)

Lucy Park: SLA note: customers expect tail latency guarantees even with many branches. They suggest a "soft deadline" where we return what we have at p99 target, then let remaining branches finish asynchronously (best-effort) if they opt in.

Maria Chen: API proposal sketch (high-level):

```
POST /v1/invoke
{
  "mode": "fan-out-conditional",    // modes: sequenced, parallel, fan-out-conditional, hedged
  "branches": [
    {"name":"validator-a","endpoint":"/validate","timeout_ms":120,"shortcircuit_on":"success"},
    {"name":"enricher-x","endpoint":"/enrichX","timeout_ms":300},
    {"name":"enricher-y","endpoint":"/enrichY","timeout_ms":300}
  ],
  "merge": {"strategy":"first_success|quorum|aggregate|weighted"},
  "retry": {"max_retries":1,"backoff_ms":50,"idempotent_hint":true},
  "billing": "per-executed-branch",
  "telemetry_tags": ["correlation_id","branch_id"]
}
```

Ajay Patel: Agree on per-branch idempotency hint; also add a correlation_id for tracing and a per-branch cancelable flag so connectors can indicate if they support cancel.

Samir Gupta: Semantics we need to lock down:
- shortcircuit: should it cancel inflight branches or just stop launching new ones? Default should be cancel to hit latency SLOs, opt-in for best-effort to let inflight finish.
- quorum: define whether quorum counts only successful responses or also weighted scores.

Lucy Park: Launch criteria checklist (what we need before GA):
- SLA matrix doc: p50/p95/p99 for 1..8 branches with/without cancels
- 3 first-party connectors implemented (validator, enricher, external API)
- Billing docs and price examples for multi-branch traffic
- Observability: per-branch latency histograms, shortcircuit rates, retry counts
- Failure-mode guidance and recommended fallback strategies

Maria Chen: Runtime/impl notes from eng: please weigh in:
- Controller must allocate a retry/timeout budget per request so retries don't amplify cost.
- Use tracing spans per branch and a join span that records merge outcome.
- Implement a cancel RPC path; when unsupported, runtime will ignore late responses and drop tokens (but still bill if executed).

Samir Gupta: Retry policy draft:
- Default: no retry for non-idempotent branches
- Per-branch override: {max_retries, backoff_ms, idempotent_hint}
- Global budget cap: max_extra_time_ms and max_extra_tokens to limit cost

Ajay Patel: UX + API ergonomics:
- Expose preset merge strategies (first_success, quorum, aggregate) plus a custom combiner for partners.
- Expose a "deadline_ms" for the entire composite request (runtime enforces per-branch deadlines relative to it).
- Make billing transparent: show estimated cost per branch in dev console before enabling.

product-bot: created ticket INT-4763 for fanout API draft — https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INT-4763 :thumbsup:

Lucy Park: Risks & tradeoffs to call out in PRD:
- cost vs latency: more branches increase unit cost; hedging reduces tail but costs more
- ordering: we can't guarantee cross-branch side-effect ordering unless customers pick "sequenced" mode
- connector surface: retries/cancel semantics require connector opt-ins

Maria Chen: Next steps:
- Eng to prototype controller behavior "cancel vs let-run" + measurement harness
- Product to author SLA scenarios + price examples
- DevEx to draft quickstart + cost calculator
- Legal to review retry and data-handling implications for external connectors

Ajay Patel: If we can get a rough prototype in 3 weeks, we can run internal perf tests and produce the SLA matrix.

Maria Chen: Great, i'll capture these decisions in the PRD and schedule a design review next Tue. Ping me if you want to join the design session. :raised_hands:
